title: g says /g/
parentNote: Today is /g/, made right at the back of the mouth — the opposite end from /t/ and /d/. The usual trouble is that /g/ is almost impossible to say on its own without a little "uh" stuck on the end, and "guh-a-guh" never turns into "gag". Clip it as short as you can, and if a word comes out with extra beats in it, just say the whole word yourself and ask for it back. Words ending in /g/ are the easy ones to start with, so "sag" and "tag" will land before "gas" does.

activities.mouthCue: The back of your tongue bumps the roof of your mouth, right at the back. Keep it short: /g/, not "guh".
activities.prompt: Every sound so far has been at the front of your mouth. This one lives at the back.
Both are quick and both buzz. One is at the back of your mouth — that one is /g/.
Three quick taps. Find the one you make furthest back.
Now the other way round. Which one taps behind your teeth?
Hold the hiss, then finish at the back. A bag full of rocks makes a shelf sag.
Only the first sound has changed.
Now /g/ at both ends. Watch what your tongue does twice.
This time /g/ starts the word. Start at the back, end with the hiss.
Four sounds. A stag is a deer with big antlers.
No picture for this one. The letters are the only clue.
All three start the same. The last sound decides it.
Listen right to the end again.
This time it is the ending that hisses or taps.
